conviction_note: The reported quarter was effectively pre-announced on 2026-07-20 (revenue at or above the top of the $3.27-3.30bn range, adj. EBITDA above the $120-125m outlook, 11 of 13 weeks of Q4 comps disclosed), so the print itself carries little downside surprise capacity; what is left is the first FY2027 guide from a CEO six weeks in the seat, which I sign as a modest negative. The positive tilt comes almost entirely from positioning - 25.26% of a 20.47m float short, 6.97 days to cover and still building, into a 20.8% twenty-day drawdown whose only identifiable cause is a sector traffic datum - and I hold the number to +2.5 against an 8.06% event-implied move because the guide has veto power over everything else and I have no edge on where it lands inside UBS's $160-200m band.
bar: Q4 FY2026 revenue ~$831m. Two agreeing sources plus a company guide: Zacks consensus $831.12m (-4.2% y/y), https://www.newsbreak.com/zacks-investment-research-321723880/4893959864533-stay-ahead-of-the-game-with-cracker-barrel-cbrl-q4-earnings-wall-street-s-insights-on-key-metrics (2026-09-18); Investing.com preview $828.8m (2026-09-22); and the company's own 2026-07-20 statement that it will 'achieve or exceed the high end' of $3.27-3.30bn FY26 revenue, which against reported Q1-Q3 of $797.19m + $874.82m + $797.37m = $2,469.4m implies Q4 >= $830.6m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067294/000110465926085071/tm2620848d1_ex99-1.htm). The adjusted-EPS bar is NOT sourced - $0.10 (Investing), $0.16 (sweep row) and $0.20 (Zacks) all circulate - so nothing here is sized off EPS.
positioning_check: 5.17m shares short = 25.26% of a 20.47m float and 23.14% of 22.35m shares outstanding; 6.97 days to cover; prior month 5.11m, i.e. the short book is still building into the print; institutional ownership 94.60%; 20d average volume 900,421. Source https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/cbrl/statistics/, read 2026-09-22. Baseline skew_25d_vol_points is +2.27 (downside paid) but that is small next to 51% 20d realised vol, and the option book itself is call-heavy: put/call open interest 0.32 on 12,031 contracts. So the market's directional statement is weak in the options and loud in the stock loan, and those two point opposite ways.

findings.finding: Cracker Barrel pre-announced the quarter it is about to report: on 2026-07-20 it disclosed that first-eleven-week Q4 comps were restaurant -2.5% and retail +0.5% and that it now expects to 'achieve or exceed the high end' of FY26 revenue and 'exceed' its adjusted EBITDA outlook - while the Zacks consensus metric sheet dated 2026-09-18 still models Q4 restaurant comps at -3.4% and retail revenue -2.9%; for restaurant comps to reach -3.4% the final two weeks of the quarter would have had to run about -8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name pays little for the reported quarter on its own: the baseline's +1.47% (2026-03-04) and +3.52% (2025-12-09) prints were in-line-to-better quarters with no change of outlook, while the only large move, +22.56% on 2026-06-09, came with a raised FY26 revenue and adj. EBITDA range. Per the lesson that a finding inside what the company has already guided to is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect, this is sized small deliberately.
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced, and I size it accordingly. The July 20 8-K is public, so any serious holder has it; what is stale is the published consensus metric line, which two months later still carries a restaurant comp 0.9pp below the company's own disclosed eleven-week run rate and a negative retail number against a disclosed positive one. If the aggregated models had been refreshed to the disclosure, the Zacks comp estimate would read about -2.5% to -2.8% and the retail line would not be negative.
findings.independence: The Zacks metric sheet is a different source from the 8-K and is what establishes the gap: https://www.newsbreak.com/zacks-investment-research-321723880/4893959864533-stay-ahead-of-the-game-with-cracker-barrel-cbrl-q4-earnings-wall-street-s-insights-on-key-metrics (2026-09-18). UBS's 2026-09-21 note independently repeats the -2.5% eleven-week restaurant figure. Note this finding and finding 2 share the 2026-07-20 8-K for the pre-announcement fact; finding 2 does not rest on it for its size.

findings.finding: CBRL goes into this print with 25.26% of a 20.47m-share float sold short, 6.97 days to cover and the short book still growing (5.11m to 5.17m shares month on month), after a 20.8% twenty-session drawdown whose only identifiable cause is sector-wide - Placer.ai's August US dining traffic of -2.4% y/y knocked CBRL down ~11% on 2026-09-15 alongside CAKE, BLMN, EAT and PTLO - and that industry y/y statistic reads across to CBRL far more weakly than to peers because CBRL's own base quarter was boycott-collapsed: it reported Q1 FY2026 (Aug-Oct 2025) restaurant comps -4.7%, retail comps -8.5% and traffic -7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's own distribution says this name pays for positioning: median absolute reaction 7.17% over seven prints and a 22.56% move on the last one, which came with a short book of comparable size. The stage's resolved record is the more direct evidence - two shorts placed into names with 18% and 23% of float short squeezed 24% and 26%, and CBRL at 25.26% is above both.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had priced the short-side asymmetry, the option book would be put-heavy and the skew wide; instead put/call open interest is 0.32 on 12,031 contracts and the 25-delta skew is +2.27 vol points against 51% realised vol - three times as much call as put open interest on a name a quarter of whose float is short. The option market is not paying for the downside the stock loan is positioned for, and the two cannot both be right.
findings.independence: The company-level base-effect leg is documented separately by the issuer's own Q1 FY2026 release (restaurant -4.7%, retail -8.5%): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067294/000110465925119675/tm2532620d1_ex99-1.htm (2025-12-09). The sector-selling cause of the 2026-09-15 drop is reported independently at https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/blmn/news/why-up-down/bloomin-brands-cracker-barrel-the-cheesecake-factory-brinker-international-and-portillos-stocks-trade-down-what-you-need-to-know. This finding does not share a document with finding 1.

findings.finding: The first FY2027 guide comes from a CEO six weeks into the job - David Deno started 2026-08-10, his inducement options struck at $56.10 against a $45.95 spot - and the company has been running a $9.99 Crispy Homestyle Chicken value platform plus a free-kids-toy offer from 2026-08-18 to 2026-10-18, i.e. straight through the first quarter he has to guide on; UBS's published band for the FY27 adjusted EBITDA guide is $160-200m against a $181m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the only line this stock has ever paid a large number for: the 2026-06-09 raise bought +22.56%, and the 2025-09-17 print, where management reset FY2026 well below estimates, cost -7.64%. So the sign here is the one that decides the day, which is why the rest of the file is sized small against it.
findings.why_not_priced: The new-CEO reset argument is in the wire and is priced; what is not is the specific resolution. Reading the two facts together - a CEO with no ownership of the FY27 plan and options 18% out of the money, and traffic currently being bought with a $9.99 entree through the guided quarter - the balance of the band sits in its lower half rather than above the $181m consensus. If the market had already settled on a lower-half guide, the consensus adjusted-EBITDA figure UBS is writing against would not still be $181m and the sell side would not have revised Q4 EPS estimates up 4.5% over the last 30 days while the stock fell 20%.
findings.independence: The CEO start date and option strike are from the company's own 8-K and Form 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067294/000110465926086902/tm2621310d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-07-27), a different source from the menu release. Resolving the two-sidedness explicitly, as the lessons file requires: the value platform is also a positive for the quarter-to-date comp, but UBS published a +3% to +4% QTD restaurant comp expectation on 2026-09-21, so that leg is already in the preview and only the margin/mix consequence is left unpriced - hence a negative sign and a modest size, not a wash.

outside_window.finding: The $9.99 fall value platform runs to 2026-10-18 and the $6-8m of cash charges from exiting Maple Street Biscuit fall across Q4 FY2026 and FY2027, so their actual comp and margin contribution is only observable at the Q1 FY2027 print in December 2026, well after this exit window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Chain-level Placer.ai or Black Box weekly traffic for CBRL in August-September 2026 - the only weekly figure findable ('traffic slid 5.3% the week of Aug. 25') traces to Restaurant Dive article 802176, which by article-ID sequence and content is the September 2025 boycott piece, not a 2026 datum; discarded on the date check
Citi's 'Sell, $42, too soon for a new CEO to have a credible strategy' note, which surfaces in 2026-dated search snippets but whose page carries 2025-09-18 - a year-old note; discarded
Any 8-K, 13D or company release between 2026-08-14 and 2026-09-22 - EDGAR shows nothing after the 2026-08-14 13G/A, so there is no company-specific cause for the 20.8% drawdown
A recoverable quarterly consensus for adjusted EPS - three sources give $0.10, $0.16 and $0.20, so no finding is sized off the EPS line
Insider open-market buying by Deno or any officer after the CEO transition - the only Form 4 activity is the grant of 3,565 RSUs and 7,434 options at $56.10 on 2026-08-10
Loyalty-member count, app download or review-volume data for CBRL later than the 12m members disclosed at Q3 FY2026
Any borrow-fee or hard-to-borrow quote for CBRL from a free source
baseline_tension: Mixed rather than clean: my positive tilt agrees with the free control (-20.8% twenty-day run-up) and with a call-heavy option book (put/call OI 0.32), but cuts against the +2.27 vol-point put skew, and the one finding that could produce a large move in either direction - the first FY2027 guide - I have signed negative, which is why the emitted number is small relative to the 8.06% event-implied move.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (a finding inside what the company already guided to is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect) cut the pre-announcement finding from +1.0 to +0.5.

Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis; an unexplained drawdown is worth 0) killed my separate +1.5 'the sector selling does not read across to CBRL' finding as a standalone item; the company-documented half of it (Q1 FY2026 comps -4.7%/-8.5% as the base) was folded into the positioning finding instead of being sized on its own, and the 'two readings of one drawdown are one finding' rule is why it is not still two entries.

Rule 7 (a crowded short is a mechanism in its own right; 18% and 23% shorts squeezed 24% and 26%) raised the positioning finding from +2.5 to +3.5, and forced the explicit sentence on why the option market's +2.27 skew is weak here - the put/call OI of 0.32.

Rule 3 (your own caveat has to reach the number) made me resolve the value-platform finding rather than leave it two-sided: the QTD-comp upside leg was published by UBS on 2026-09-21 and is priced, so only the margin/mix consequence survives and it is signed negative.

Rule 4 (financing is a question) removed an inferred negative I had drafted on the incremental rent from the 26-store sale-leaseback: the money buys debt reduction and the use of expiring capital-loss carryforwards, the cap rate is not in any document, and 'documents beat inference' says an inferred rent number is not a finding.

Rule 6 also forced me to state that the adjusted-EPS bar is unsourced across three disagreeing numbers, so nothing is sized off EPS; the revenue bar is sourced to a company guide plus two agreeing estimates and carries the print_vs_bar number.
Net effect: findings 4 to 3, sum +3.5 to +2.5, expected move +3.0 to +2.5, print_vs_bar +1.2 to +1.5.
